content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999 (we can't check price but assume buyable). Need to output JSON route.

We have target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We need to break it into precursors using templates. We have some templates found: template 38653 gave two possible precursors (both not buyable). Template 1037371 gives a precursor: O=C(O)/C=C/... which is a long chain with a carboxylic acid attached to a phenyl? Actually product is our target; reactant is O=C(O)/C=C/... which is a polyunsaturated chain attached to a cyclic sugar? Wait.

But we can design a synthetic plan: The target appears to be a glycoside (a sugar ring) with a side chain: a polyunsaturated chain (C=C/C=C/C(O)=O) attached via an ether to the sugar. Also there is another side chain: /C=C(CO)/C attached via ether.

Thus we could think of disconnection at the ether bonds: break the O-glycosidic link to give the sugar (a protected diol?) and the allylic alcohol side chain (maybe an allylic alcohol). The sugar core is a tetrahydrofuran? Actually O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C... This is a 5-membered ring (furanose) with two O-alkyl substituents.

Simplify: The sugar is a 1,3-diol cyclic (maybe a methylated ribose). The side chains are unsaturated acids/alcohols.

We can propose retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of the ether linking the side chain (C=C(CO)/C) to the sugar. Use a template that breaks ether to give sugar hydroxyl and allylic alcohol (C=C(CO)C). The allylic alcohol is commercially available (C=C(CO)C is 3-buten-1-ol? Actually C=C(CO)C is 2-methyl-2-propen-1-ol? Wait SMILES C=C(CO)C is isobut-2-en-1-ol (3-methyl-2-propen-1-ol). That's buyable (we saw True). Good.

The sugar fragment after breaking both ethers would be the cyclic diol (maybe a protected sugar). The other side chain is the polyunsaturated acid: C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O is trans-2,4-hexadienoic acid? Actually SMILES C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O is trans-2,4-pentadienoic acid? Let's count: C (CH3) - /C=C/ - C = C - C(O)=O. That's trans-2,4-pentadienoic acid (trans, trans). That is also buyable (True). So we can break both ether bonds to give sugar diol and two side chains.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> sugar diol + allylic alcohol + unsaturated acid via two ether formation steps (glycosylation). Could be done sequentially.

We need to find templates for ether formation (reverse of ether cleavage). The template 38653 is reverse of ether formation: it shows retro_smarts_template: [C:1]/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[C:4]>>[C:1]-[C@@H;D3;+0:2]1-O-[C@H;D3;+0:3]-1-[C:4] . So forward reaction is forming the double bond from cyclic ether? Actually retro template shows product (target) is double bond; reactant is cyclic ether. So applying this template to target gives precursors that are cyclic ether (sugar) and alkene chain. That's what we got: two precursors (both not buyable). But maybe we can apply again to break second ether? The template gave two possible precursors each with one side chain still attached? Let's examine the two precursors:

1) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C[C@@H]2O[C@H]2/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

This still has a sugar with one side chain (the polyunsaturated acid) attached via ether, plus a terminal allylic alcohol (CO). Actually this precursor still contains the sugar and the polyunsaturated acid attached, plus a terminal allylic alcohol (CO). So we need another disconnection to break the remaining ether.

2) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

Similar.

Thus we can apply same template again to break the second ether, yielding sugar diol and both side chains.

Let's try applying template 38653 to one of those precursors.
